bib.title: Stealing Part of a Production Language Model
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235, 2024

question: How much information can an adversary learn about a black-box production language model by querying its API?
hypothesis: The final layer of a language model projects from hidden dimension h to a larger logit space, so it is low-rank and its width (and the layer up to symmetries) can be recovered from API queries that expose logits, logprobs or logit bias.
contributions: A top-down model-stealing attack that recovers the embedding projection layer (up to symmetries) and hidden dimension of a transformer from API access
Logit-recovery methods for APIs exposing top-K logprobs with logit bias, top-1 with binary logit bias, and logprob-free logit-bias APIs
Application to OpenAI ada, babbage, babbage-002, gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct and gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 with permission, plus defenses and mitigations

method.summary: Query the model on many random prefixes, recover the full logit vector for each (directly in a strawman logits API, or via logit-bias queries against a top-5 logprobs API), stack them in a matrix Q and take an SVD. The number of numerically significant singular values (largest multiplicative gap) gives the hidden dimension h; U*Sigma gives the projection matrix W up to an h x h linear transform G. Validated on six open models, then run on five OpenAI models with OpenAI's permission.
method.task: Model extraction (high-fidelity) of the final embedding projection layer of a transformer LM

other.use: only the LayerNorm-vs-RMSNorm detection stress test via released logprobs (App. B.2.2)

inference.decoding: Logit-bias attack on OpenAI APIs: biases of B on 4 tokens plus a reference token; top-5 logprobs read. Logprob-free variants use temperature 0 / argmax.
inference.samples: inferred: one query batch per random prefix; n > h prefixes needed (Pythia-1.4B figure uses 1024-3072 queries); production runs < 2e6 to < 4e7 queries for dimension
inference.prompting: Random prefixes (RandPrefix()); the exact prefix distribution and length are not stated

parameters.logit_bias_B: large value; OpenAI limits are 300 tokens per request and bias in [-100, 100]
parameters.attack_chosen_for_production: logprob-4 (Section 5.3, 4 logits per query via reference token), with 0.25 queries per logit
parameters.cost-optimal_variant: force token x repeated m times with bias B on x and B' < B on four others; query cost 1/(4m), token cost (1+m)/(4m)

other.numerical_rank: largest multiplicative gap between consecutive singular values

metrics.name: Stolen hidden size
metrics.definition: index of the largest multiplicative gap lambda_i / lambda_{i+1} in singular values of Q

metrics.name: W RMS
metrics.definition: root mean square between actual W and extracted W~ after solving a least-squares h x h affine alignment W~ G ≈ W

metrics.name: Bits of precision (logit validation)
metrics.definition: average bits of agreement between true and recovered logit vector

metrics.name: Queries per logit
metrics.definition: amortized API queries to recover one logit

baselines: RMS between a randomly initialized model and actual weights: 2e-2
eval.protocol: Six open models with full logits; logit-estimation attacks compared on a limited-query interface (Table 4); five OpenAI models available on 1 January 2024 with OpenAI's advance permission, sizes confirmed by OpenAI. No seeds or repeated trials stated.

availability.code: Supplementary code for logprob-free attacks: github.com/dpaleka/stealing-part-lm-supplementary; Colab notebook for orthogonal recovery (App. H)
availability.data: Extracted logprobs/weights deleted after the attack (and GPT-3.5 logprobs deleted for security)

results.claim: Abstract: the exact gpt-3.5-turbo hidden dimension was recovered and the full matrix is estimated at under $2,000.
On six open models the dimension is recovered with error 0 or 1 in five of six cases (error up to 2 reported for LLaMA); the exception is GPT-2 Small at 757 vs 768, explained by effective rank.
results.setup: Full logits API, GPT-2 Small/XL, Pythia 1.4B/6.9B, LLaMA 7B/65B
results.quote: our attack reports a hidden dimension of 757

results.setup: Six open models, logits API, after h x h affine alignment

results.claim: Logit-estimation precision and cost: logprob-4 (top-5, reference token) is best, 23.0 bits at 0.25 queries per logit.
results.setup: Logit validation, top-5 logprobs with logit bias; other rows: logprob-5 11.5 bits/0.64; logprob-1 6.1 bits/1.0; binary search 7.2/10.0; hyperrectangle 15.7/5.4; one-of-n 18.0/3.7 (no logprobs)
results.table: Table 4, row logprob-4 (§5.3), column Bits of precision

results.claim: The best logprob-free attack gets 18 bits at 3.7 queries per logit and is within a factor of two of an information-theoretic lower bound.
results.setup: Logprob-free API with logit bias, one-of-n attack; lower bound assumes i.i.d. uniform logits
results.quote: recovers 18 bits of precision at just 3.7 queries per logit

results.claim: Allowing both logit bias and logprobs makes the attack about 10x cheaper than logprob-free.
results.setup: Stated as motivation for the 'logit bias XOR logprobs' mitigation

results.claim: 8-bit and 4-bit quantisation of Llama-7B does not change the recovered dimension or the number of queries needed.
results.quote: We observe no meaningful differences at different levels of quantization

limits: Recovers one layer only (embedding projection) and only up to an h x h transform; exact W is impossible for transformers with residual connections (Lemma 4.2(ii)); an efficient algorithm exists only for affine ambiguity, an orthogonal-ambiguity method needs O(h^2) equations and O(h^6) time and was shown only on Pythia-14M
'We see no obvious methodology to extend it beyond just a single layer'
Threat model assumes a perfect oracle without timing or implementation leakage

Full-matrix extraction was only run on ada and babbage; babbage-002 and gpt-3.5 full-matrix costs are estimates (dagger/plus in Table 3); gpt-3.5-turbo sizes withheld at OpenAI's request, so not independently checkable
Only five OpenAI models were tested because only these received advance permission; no ablation of other attack variants on production APIs
The attack was disclosed and OpenAI and Google changed their APIs; logit bias affecting top logprobs was removed, so attacks as described no longer work as-is (dated)
Logprob-free lower bound assumes i.i.d. uniform logits, which is unrealistic
Assumes rank h for hidden matrix and W; GPT-2 Small shows effective rank 757 in lower precision (rank gap fits float64 only after tiny singular values)
Authors say there are no immediate practical consequences of learning this layer

problems: The abstract and intro describe gpt-3.5 costs ('under $200', 'under $2,000') more loosely than Table 3 ($800 for turbo-1106 dimension, $8,000 estimated matrix).
The paper does not state explicitly whether the Table 3 dollar figures for ada/babbage were billed or computed from token counts; only dagger/plus entries are flagged as not run/estimated.
Value of logit bias B and the random prefix distribution are not stated.
